name: Friday Night Ride
schedule: Fridays in season, evening. The start and time change week to week and are on each calendar event; starts stay near the waterfront or a subway stop. Next listed: Fri Oct 2, 2026, 6:00 pm from Riverdale Park East, 33 km, ending on the Danforth.
season: summer and early fall; no Friday rides listed after Oct 2, 2026
pace: Urban Roller class, 16–22 km/h, stops to regroup
cost: free for guests this season (register first)
visitor_notes: Guests ride free but must register on the TBN calendar before the ride; if you haven't registered you may not join. Helmet and front and rear lights required. Not a beginner ride: you should be able to hold about 20 km/h on city streets.
description: The Toronto Bicycling Network's social Friday evening ride: festivals, the waterfront, Toronto Island, the Distillery District, the Brick Works. 20 to 35 km at a relaxed pace with regroups, and most riders stay for food and a drink after. Starts move each week.
evidence: TBN's calendar lists a Friday Night Ride on Fri Oct 2, 2026, 6:00 pm from 450 Broadview Ave, open to guest riders for free (fetched Sept 30, 2026).

refresh.notes: Each ride is its own Wild Apricot event (tbn.ca/event-<id>) with start, time and guest registration. The club-wide list of the next 20 events is https://www.tbn.ca/Next20events.

name: Saturday Morning Ride
schedule: Saturdays, early April to late October, 9:30 am sharp, back by 12:30 or 1:00 pm. The start changes weekly and is on each calendar event, usually near a subway or transit stop. 2026 dates left: Oct 3, 10, 17, 24 and 31 (the season's final ride).

start_location.name: Changes weekly (Oct 3, 2026: Shoppers World parking lot)
start_location.address: Victoria Park Ave & Danforth Ave, Toronto, ON

pace: Urban Roller class, 19–23 km/h average, 30–60 km
founded_note: Run by the same two coordinators since 2013.
visitor_notes: Club ride. Non-members can buy TBN's $15 30-day trial, which covers most rides; everyone registers on the calendar before each ride. Helmet and a spare tube required. Find the ride leader and say you're new.
description: TBN's in-town Saturday ride on Toronto's paved trails and quiet streets: the Martin Goodman Trail, the Don, the Leslie Street Spit, the Humber, Edwards Gardens. Fifteen rotating routes, 30 to 60 km, groups of about 15 to 35. You're done by early afternoon.
evidence: The program page lists Saturday rides at 9:30 am on Oct 3, 10, 17, 24 and 31, 2026, with Oct 31 marked the final ride of 2026 (fetched Sept 30, 2026).

refresh.notes: Season ends Oct 31, 2026; the 2027 dates appear on the same page in spring.

name: Sunday Leisure Wheeler
schedule: Sundays, late April to early October (2026 rides listed to Oct 18), usually 10:00 am. The start changes weekly and is on each calendar event. Next: Oct 4 from Oriole Park, Oct 11 at 10:10 am from June Rowlands Park, Oct 18 from Aurora GO station.

start_location.name: Changes weekly (Oct 4, 2026: Oriole Park)
start_location.address: Oriole Park, west of Davisville Station, south of Chaplin Cres., Toronto, ON

pace: 15–18 km/h, 18–55 km, frequent stops to regroup
visitor_notes: Registration opens the Monday before each ride and runs six days. Non-members use TBN's $15 30-day trial. Arrive 15 minutes early. Check the schedule after 8:00 am on ride day for weather cancellations.
description: TBN's slow Sunday ride, built for entry-level riders, people coming back to cycling after a long break, and seniors. Paved trails and streets at 15 to 18 km/h with frequent regroups. Bring lunch on the longer ones.
evidence: The program page lists Leisure Wheeler rides on Sun Oct 4, 11 and 18, 2026 (fetched Sept 30, 2026).

refresh.notes: Upcoming rides are listed at the foot of the program page; the season closes in October.

name: Critical Mass Toronto
schedule: Last Friday of the month. The Sept 25, 2026 ride met at 6:00 pm and rolled at 6:30 pm. The start moves month to month (Aug 28, 2026: Prince Edward Viaduct Parkette; Sept 25, 2026: High Park front gates on Bloor St W).

start_location.name: Changes monthly; check the latest announcement

visitor_notes: No sign-up. The start point moves, so check the month's announcement first. Bring lights: from September the ride ends in the dark.
description: Toronto's monthly mass ride. In 2026 it doubled as a protest against the province's bike lane removals and drew big crowds: more than 1,000 riders in August, when the mayor spoke at the start, and 783 counted bikes in September. Slow pace, one big group, music and costumes.
evidence: Two local bike blogs write up the Aug 28 and Sept 25, 2026 rides (both last Fridays), and an eBikes International post gives the Sept 25 meet time and place (fetched Sept 30, 2026).

refresh.notes: No official site. Local bike blogs (jnyyz.wordpress.com, twowheeledpolitics.ca) write up each month's ride; the start is announced shortly before. In August 2026 Cycle Toronto was among the groups that helped put it on.

name: Bike Rally Training Rides
schedule: Weekend training rides from April to July, 8:00 am (arrive 15 minutes early for sign-in). Mostly Saturdays, some Sundays. The start and route change each week; 2026 starts included Kipling station and Vaughan Metropolitan Centre station. Outdoor rides begin again in April 2027.
season: April to July, before the August Rally

start_location.name: Changes weekly (listed on each calendar event)

visitor_notes: Run for riders training for the August Bike Rally. The pages don't say whether riders who haven't registered for the Rally can join, so email the Rally first. Some rides include a box lunch at the break ($10, cash or tap, 2026).
description: Weekly long training rides for the Friends For Life Bike Rally, the August ride from Toronto to Montréal that raises money for PWA (600 km, with 300 km and 100 km options). Routes head out of the city to places like Burlington, Glen Williams and Keswick, with a sign-in and announcements at the start. Montréal and Kingston riders have their own training rides.
evidence: The Rally's calendar holds 2026 Toronto training rides into late July (Vaughan to Keswick, Sat July 25, 2026, 8:00 am), and the training page says organized outdoor rides begin in April (fetched Sept 30, 2026).

refresh.notes: Squarespace calendar; each event has its own ICS link (append ?format=ical to the event URL) but the collection has no feed. 2027 training rides should appear from March.

name: Thursday MTB Group Ride
schedule: Thursdays, 6:00 pm, through the fall. Slow, medium and fast groups; 90 to 120 minutes in the Don Valley. Cancelled for rain.
pace: Slow, medium and fast groups; the slow group leaves no rider behind
visitor_notes: 18 and older, with some mountain bike experience. Sign the waiver online before you come. Rental bikes must be booked in advance. Lights are mandatory this fall. Park on Canvarco Road or in the nearby plazas.
description: Bateman's leads free Thursday evening mountain bike rides from its Leaside trail shop into the Don Valley's singletrack. Riders split by ability, and the slow group is about trail etiquette and building confidence. Snacks and drinks at the shop after.
evidence: Bateman's group-ride page advertises fall Thursday 6:00 pm rides from the trail shop and says lights are now required; nothing on it is dated (fetched Sept 30, 2026).

refresh.notes: The site banner carries the current ride night; rain cancellations are posted on the shop's Instagram.
